title: Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary: A Guide to Salary Package Rent and Take-Home Pay

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a full-time employee on 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, the annual gross is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool for quick results.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage ($26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026) applies to employees not covered by an award or enterprise agreement. bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Salary

Understanding how your hourly rate translates to an annual salary is essential for budgeting, negotiating pay, and planning your finances. The basic formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role based on a 38-hour week, the calculation is:

**Annual gross salary = hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks**

This gives you a figure before tax, Medicare, and superannuation. For example, if you earn $30 per hour, your annual gross is $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. If you work part-time or casual hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. Our [timesheet](/) tool lets you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading.

### Understanding the National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

Australia’s National Minimum Wage (NMW) from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. This rate applies to employees not covered by a modern award or enterprise agreement. However, most workers are covered by an award that sets higher minimum pay rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award, listing minimum hourly rates, allowances, and penalty rates. Always check your award to ensure you’re being paid correctly. If you’re unsure which award applies, use the Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay and Conditions Tool () to find your minimum entitlements.

### The Role of Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. For the NMW, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). When using our timesheet, you can check a box to add 25% casual loading. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading; the tool adds it automatically. For award-covered casuals, the loading may vary, so refer to the relevant [pay guides](/blog).

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your salary. From 1 July 2026, the Super Guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This means if your annual gross is $60,000, your employer contributes an additional $7,200 to your super fund. Super is not deducted from your pay; it’s an extra benefit. Our calculator estimates super at 12% but stops at the cap. For more on salary packaging and super, see [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Tax and Medicare: What You Keep

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy. The tax-free threshold is $18,200, then:
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a 2% Medicare levy (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). For example, on a $59,280 salary, your tax is approximately $7,684 and Medicare $1,186, leaving about $50,410 after tax. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page for detailed estimates.

### Salary Package Rent and Other Considerations

The term “salary package rent” refers to an arrangement where your employer pays your rent from your pre-tax salary, reducing your taxable income. This is common in not-for-profit sectors and can boost your take-home pay. However, our calculator does not account for salary packaging, including rent, or other deductions like HELP loans or the Medicare levy surcharge. Always consult a tax professional for personalised advice. For more on salary packaging, visit [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Using the Fortnightly View

If you’re paid fortnightly, multiply your weekly pay by two. For a 38-hour week at $30 per hour, your weekly gross is $1,140, so fortnightly is $2,280. This can help with budgeting and comparing job offers. Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool provides both weekly and fortnightly figures.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For accurate award rates, always refer to the Fair Work Ombudsman’s [pay guides](/blog) and the Pay and Conditions Tool (). The National Minimum Wage and award rates are legally enforceable, and your employer must pay at least the minimum. If you have questions about your pay, contact the Fair Work Ombudsman.
